Author: Hirdesh Bench: Hirdesh  NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4799  1   IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT GWALIOR  BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE HIRDESH  ON THE 5 th OF FEBRUARY, 2026  MISC.

sentences.text: APPEAL No. 1147 of 2015  GIRJA AND OTHERS  Versus  ASHOK AND OTHERS  Appearance:
Shri Bhupendra Singh Dhakad - Advocate for the appellant  Shri Arvind Kumar Agrawal- Advocate for respondent No.3.

ORDER This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellants/claimants challenging the award dated 13.08.2015 passed by the Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sabalgarh, District Morena (M.P.) in Claim Case No.47/2013,
whereby the claim petition filed by the appellants/claimants was rejected.

entities.text: Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sabalgarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 28.09.2011 at about 11:30 p.m., the complainant Suresh and the deceased Dashrath were travelling towards Sabalgarh on a tractor.

After stopping the tractor on the roadside, while Dashrath was urinating, a Mahindra tractor bearing Registration No.
RJ-34/RA-0218 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner, overturned, and its trolley turned turtle, as a result of which Dashrath was buried underneath and sustained fatal injuries.
He was immediately taken to Sabalgarh Hospital, where he was declared dead.
A report of the incident was lodged at Police Station Sabalgarh, pursuant to which Crime No.292/2011 under Section 304- A of the IPC was registered.
During investigation, the offending tractor was seized, the driver Ashok Dhakad was arrested, and after completion of investigation, a charge- sheet was filed against him.

The appellants thereafter filed a claim petition seeking NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:4799 2 MA-1147-2015 compensation.
The respondents filed their written statements and denied the averments made in the claim petition.
3. After framing issues and recording evidence of both the parties, the Claims Tribunal rejected the claim petition, holding that the involvement of the alleged offending vehicle was not established.

Girja vs Ashok on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83984988/
1 4.

Being aggrieved, the appellants have preferred this appeal contending that the learned Claims Tribunal committed a grave error of law in dismissing the claim petition without proper appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence available on record.

It is submitted that the testimony of eye-witness Suresh (PW-2), duly corroborated by police records, clearly establishes that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the Mahindra tractor bearing Registration No. RJ-34/RA-0218.

It is further contended that the minor discrepancy in the tractor number was satisfactorily explained during investigation and duly clarified by the Investigating Officer, and that the respondents failed to adduce any rebuttal evidence.
Hence, the impugned award deserves to be set aside.
5 . Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company opposed the appeal and prayed for its dismissal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.
On perusal of the record, it is found that the accident occurred on 28.09.2011 and merg intimation was registered in the intervening night of 28/29.09.2011 at 00:45 hours.

As per merg intimation (Ex. A-3), informant Suresh reported that a Mahindra tractor was being driven rashly and negligently, due to which its pedal broke, the trolley overturned upon Dashrath, and he succumbed to injuries.
After inquiry, FIR (Ex. A-2) was registered, wherein the registration number of the offending vehicle was mentioned as RJ-34-RA-0216.

However, after completion of investigation, charge- sheet was filed against the driver Ashok Dhakad in respect of tractor bearing NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4799 3 MA-1147-2015 Registration No.
RJ-34-RA-0218.
8.

So far as the contention of learned counsel for the appellants regarding the discrepancy in the registration number of the offending vehicle is concerned, it is borne out from the record that the Investigating Officer, who inquired into and investigated the matter, has categorically stated that due to an inadvertent clerical mistake, the registration number of the offending tractor was mentioned as 0216 in the statement of witness Babulal.

However, the said error was subsequently rectified when the Investigating Officer recorded the statement under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, wherein the correct registration number of the tractor was mentioned as 0218.

9. Investigating Officer- Dashrath Singh Yadav, who was examined by the Insurance Company clearly gave the statement and elaborately discussed each and every fact how and which manner registration number of the offending vehicle was wrongfully mentioned in FIR which was corrected by him at the time of filing charge sheet.
10.
In view of the aforesaid evidence, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Claims Tribunal committed a manifest error in holding that the accident was not caused by the offending vehicle.
The finding recorded by the Claims Tribunal on this aspect is contrary to the material available on record and is not sustainable in the eye of law.
The appellants have successfully established that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the Mahindra tractor bearing Registration No. RJ-34-RA-0218.

Girja vs Ashok on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83984988/
2 11.

On perusal of the impugned award, it is further found that since the claim petition was dismissed on the ground of non-involvement of the vehicle, the Claims Tribunal did not assess the quantum of compensation payable to the appellants.
12. Accordingly, the impugned award dated 13.08.2015 passed by the Claims Tribunal is hereby set aside.
The matter is remanded back to the Claims Tribunal for determination of compensation and liability in accordance with law.

The Claims NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4799 4 MA-1147-2015 Tribunal is directed to afford opportunity to both the parties to lead evidence, if any,
on the question of quantum and liability and thereafter decide the claim afresh.
13. The Claims Tribunal shall endeavour to dispose of the matter expeditiously, preferably within a period of six months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
14. The parties are directed to appear before the Claims Tribunal on 20.02.2026 , and thereafter on such dates as may be fixed by the Claims Tribunal.
15. With the aforesaid directions, the miscellaneous appeal is allowed, and the matter stands remanded.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
